newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end up with firm cash,shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end up with firm cash,shortcovering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended significantly higher Thursday, propped up by technical shortcovering and slightly firmer cash prices, industry sources said.

October finished 4.5 cents higher at $1.809 per million British thermal units. November settled up 5.2 cents at $1.989 after hitting a high of $2.015 earlier. Other deffereds were also higher, with most strength seen in the front months.
"Cash really isn't cratering, and there's uncertainty over the weather," said one futures trader, adding he saw more upside potential for October.
October broke through its narrow trading channel, widening it only slightly as the front month reached a session high of $1.84.
Traders said support in the prompt month was in the $1.72-1.73 area and then at $1.68. Resistance was seen first at $1.85, then $1.955.

Despite recent strength in October, other traders thought much more upside potential was unlikely, with the main factor targetted at the weather. Next week's forecasts are calling for normal to below-normal temperatures throughout most of the eastern U.S. and Texas. Further out, temperatures are expected to be below-normal in the East and the Great Lakes states.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes touched the $1.70 level in late trading, with Henry Hub physicals climbing to as high as the mid-$1.70s. Midcontinent prices were stable in the mid-to-high $1.50s.
NYMEX said an estimated 34,453 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 23,074, which could add steam to the upward movement, traders said.
NYMEX's October Permian contract settled two cents lower at $1.50. An estimated 19 trades exchanged hands.
On the KCBT, October finished 2.5 cents higher at $1.575. Other front months made similar gains. The East/West spread widened by 2.4 cents to 23.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha were talked in the $1.56-$1.60 range, down a couple of cents from Wednesday.
